Lessons.Title: Solving Quadratics
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Explain (in writing) the reasoning used to solve a quadratic equation by completing the square and by using the quadratic formula. Justify whether two radical expressions are equivalent. Solve quadratic equations and explain the solution method.
Move the constant and complete square to solve; compare with quadratic formula and substitute roots into the original quadratic.

Source activity 16.1: Find the Perfect Squares: The expression \(x^2+8x+16\) is equivalent to \((x+4)^2\). Which expressions are equivalent to \((x+n)^2\) for some number \(n\)? Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 16.2: Different Ways to Solve It: Elena and Han solved the equation \(x^2-6x+7=0\) in different ways. Elena said, “First I added 2 to each side: \(\displaystyle x^2 - 6x + 7 + 2 = 2\) \(\displaystyle (x - 3)^2 = 2\) I can find the square roots of both sides: \(\displaystyle x - 3 = \pm \sqrt{2}\) Which is the same as: \(\displaystyle x = 3 \pm \sqrt{2}\) So the two solutions are \(x=3+\sqrt{2}\) and… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 16.3: Solve These Ones: Solve each quadratic equation with the method of your choice. Be prepared to compare your approach with a partner‘s. \(x^2 - 10x + 25 = 0\) \(x^2 + 14x + 40 = 0\) \(x^2 + 14x + 39 = 0\) \(3x^2 - 5x - 11 = 0\) Consider the quadratic equation: \(\displaystyle x^2 - 5x = 25\) It is often most efficient to solve equations like this by completing the square. To complete the square,… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.
